intro: On Isola San Nicola, the island of the Tremiti that carries the abbey and fortress, Puglia's register of monumental trees protects a small group of ombu, an evergreen tree from the South American pampas with a swollen, buttressed base. Two visitors recorded them there in August 2025, about 18 metres apart. Ferries and hydrofoils reach the island in summer from Termoli, Vieste, Peschici and Rodi Garganico.
meta_description: The ombu of Isola San Nicola in the Tremiti islands, a South American tree on Puglia's register of monumental trees.

trees.name: Ombu of San Nicola, Isole Tremiti
trees.story:
A tree from the Argentine pampas grows on a rock in the Adriatic. The ombu, Phytolacca dioica, is native to South America, and Puglia's register of monumental trees lists a group of them on Isola San Nicola, the fortified island of the Tremiti, on sheet 01/E363/FG/16.

The register calls it a homogeneous group rather than one tree, and it gives no girth, no height and no age. What it records is that ombu here are worth protecting. The species is an odd one to find on a Mediterranean island, evergreen, with a swollen, buttressed base, and it stands up well to sea wind.

The proof that they are still there is recent. In August 2025 two visitors, three weeks apart, logged an ombu on San Nicola on iNaturalist, each identification confirmed by a second person, and their two records fall about 18 metres apart and within about 30 metres of where the register places it. That points to one small cluster.

What we cannot tell you yet is whether that spot is on a public path or inside a closed part of the abbey and fortress that cover the island. Ferries and hydrofoils run to San Nicola in summer from Termoli, Vieste, Peschici and Rodi Garganico, thinning out outside May to September.

Nobody has published an age for these trees. If you go, tell us which trunk is biggest and how you reached it.
trees.how_to_recognise: You can recognise it by the base, swollen and buttressed, on an evergreen tree from South America. It stands in a small cluster of ombu on Isola San Nicola, the island of the abbey and fortress.
trees.access: Island of San Nicola is open to visitors by ferry/hydrofoil (Termoli, Vieste, Peschici, Rodi Garganico, Manfredonia in season). Whether the exact tree stands on a public path or inside a paid or closed part of the abbey-fortress complex is NOT established; flagged.
trees.transport: Ferry or hydrofoil to San Nicola in summer from Termoli, Vieste, Peschici and Rodi Garganico (about 45 to 90 minutes depending on port); services thin out outside May to September. Over 30 minutes, so an island day trip, not a walk from the coast.

question_meta: The Tremiti's registered trees are a group of ombu on Isola San Nicola. Nobody has dated them.
question_answer: No tree we map on the Tremiti has a published age. Puglia's register lists a group of ombu, Phytolacca dioica, on Isola San Nicola, and two visitors recorded them there in August 2025.

Two iNaturalist records from August 2025, each confirmed by a second person, fall within about 30 metres of the register's point. Whether that spot is on a public path or inside a closed part of the abbey and fortress we have not established. The ombu is native to the South American pampas, an evergreen with a swollen, buttressed base that stands up well to sea wind, which makes a group of them on an Adriatic island an oddity worth the register's protection. The two observers' records lie about 18 metres apart, so the trees most likely form one small cluster rather than being scattered over the island. faq.a: Phytolacca dioica, an evergreen tree native to South America, known for its swollen, buttressed base and its tolerance of sea wind.

faq.q: How do I get to Isola San Nicola?
faq.a: By ferry or hydrofoil in summer from Termoli, Vieste, Peschici or Rodi Garganico, about 45 to 90 minutes depending on the port. Services thin out outside May to September.

faq.q: Can I walk right up to the trees?
faq.a: We have not established whether they stand on a public path or inside a closed part of the abbey and fortress.
